How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Reputation

Adverse items are attributed to their sources and need one primary source or two independent ones before they are published.

Reputation
Regulatory actionsAlphabet disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K and its Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026: a European Commission decision in September 2025 fining Google EUR 3.0 billion over advertising technology, which Google appealed; a Japan Fair Trade Commission cease-and-desist order in April 2025 over Android agreements; a settlement with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission approved in December 2025; the EUR 4.1 billion Android fine becoming final in July 2026, with a US$5.2 billion payment; and Digital Markets Act non-compliance decisions in July 2026 with fines of EUR 430 million (Google Play) and EUR 460 million (Search), appealed in October 2026. Computerworld and the Irish Examiner reported on 2025-12-09 that the European Commission opened an antitrust investigation into Google's use of publisher content and YouTube videos for its AI models. None of these is attributed to the Gemini API, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform or Gemini Enterprise as enterprise services. Pricing

Pricing is usually not public. This states what is known, what is estimated, and what is not public.

Pricing
KnownGemini Developer API, paid tier, per million tokens: Gemini 4 Carbon US$2.00 input and US$10.00 output through 30 November 2026, then US$4.00 and US$20.00. Gemini 4 Carbon is not on the free tier.; Grounding with Google Search on Gemini 3 and newer models: 5,000 free requests a month, then US$14 per 1,000 requests.; Gemini API billing tiers carry a spend cap; Tier 1 is capped at US$250.; Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: usage-based. Models are billed per token under standard pay-as-you-go, discounted Flex, premium Priority, or Provisioned Throughput subscriptions; agent infrastructure is metered by compute, memory and storage. Agent Search document retrieval is about US$4.00 per 1,000 queries plus index storage. Pipelines start at US$0.03 per run.; Gemini Enterprise at launch, as reported by TechCrunch on 2025-10-09: Standard and Plus editions from US$30 per seat per month on annual plans; Business edition US$21 per seat per month.; Google Cloud support: Enhanced and Premium plans are charged as a percentage of monthly cloud spend with minimums; Gemini Enterprise Standard, Plus and Frontline include baseline support at no extra cost. Questions to ask the vendor (2)

  1. Have any large or regulated customers stopped using Gemini models, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform or Gemini Enterprise in the last two years, and why?
    Departures of large customers can signal service or commercial problems.
  2. Have there been any leadership departures, governance disputes or conduct findings affecting Google Cloud or Google DeepMind leadership in the last two years?
    Leadership disputes or departures can disrupt a critical supplier's strategy.

Timeline

  1. 2026-10-13 · launch Google
    Google releases the Gemini 4 model family

    Google's deprecations schedule lists the release of Gemini 4 Argon on 13 October 2026, followed by Gemini 4 Carbon on 10 November, Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November and Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026. Google describes Carbon as its strongest reasoning model, with a 1M-token context window, and published a model card for it on 10 November 2026. Introductory pricing for Carbon runs to 30 November 2026.   2. 2026-09-01 · litigation Google
    US court denies divestiture in Google advertising technology case, orders behavioural remedies

    Alphabet disclosed in its Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026 that in September 2026 the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia issued its remedies decision in the Department of Justice advertising technology case, denying structural divestitures and ordering behavioural remedies on interoperability, data access and auction conduct. Alphabet said it plans to appeal the adverse part of the April 2025 liability decision once final judgment is entered.   22. 2025-06-12 · outage Google
    Google Cloud APIs disrupted worldwide by a Service Control policy fault

    Google stated in its incident report that from 10:51 to 18:18 US/Pacific on 12 June 2025 many Google Cloud products were disrupted across regions. Google attributed it to a quota-policy change containing blank fields that crashed its Service Control API management binary through a code path, added on 29 May 2025, that had not been exercised during rollout; Google said recovery began within about 40 minutes but took up to about 2 hours 40 minutes in us-central1 because restarting tasks overloaded the underlying infrastructure. The Vertex Gemini API, Agent Platform Online Inference and Agent Search are listed among the affected products. Google said it froze changes to the system and would make it fail open.
